name: ADA4627-1 / ADA4637-1 (ADI single JFET-input; ADA4637-1 decompensated)
tagline: ADI's 2009 JFET-input single (6.1 nV/rtHz, 19 MHz), often suggested as an OPA627 alternative. ADI's own AN-1429 names it among op amps 'reputable with music fans'.
technology: JFET-input single op amp. ADI calls the ADA4637-1 'a decompensated version of the ADA4627-1', stable at a noise gain of 5 or greater. The ADA4627-1 is therefore the unity-gain-stable member (inferred from that wording). Title history: the ADA4627-1 product page is titled '36 V, 19 MHz, Low Noise, Low Bias Current, JFET Op Amp'. An early ADA4637 datasheet copy is titled '36 V, 80 MHz, Low Noise, Low Bias Current, JFET Op Amp'. The current combined datasheet (Rev. F) is titled '30 V, High Speed, Low Noise, Low Bias Current, JFET Operational Amplifier'. The process technology was not verified.

The SPICE model v1.0 is dated 08/2010. An early standalone ADA4637 datasheet ('36 V, 80 MHz ...', copy on Octopart) appears to predate the merged ADA4627-1/ADA4637-1 datasheet; that sequence is inferred from the titles.

key_specs.value: ±5 V to ±15 V dual supply (operating). Titles: '36 V' on the product page and early datasheets, '30 V' on the Rev. F datasheet. The SPICE 'Generic Desc' gives '8/30V'.
key_specs.source: ADI product description via web search (https://www.analog.com/en/products/ada4627-1.html); datasheet titles; ADI SPICE header. The 36 V figure is probably the absolute-maximum rating (inference).
ADI Eagle library devices; ordering codes ARZ/BRZ/ACPZ; Mouser listing for ADA4637-1ARZ

key_specs.value: The blog claim of higher slew rate and bandwidth than the OPA627 is marginally consistent for the ADA4627-1 (60 V/us vs. the OPA627's commonly cited 55 V/us, not verified this run). It is clearly true for the ADA4637-1 (170 V/us).

reputation.summary: ADI's application note AN-1429 lists the ADA4627-1, alongside the AD797, OP275 and AD8620, as ADI op amps 'reputable with music fans'. That is vendor marketing, not a measurement. Enthusiast material carried over from the discovery notes was not re-verified: a diyAudio thread titled 'ADA4627 outperforms Burr-Brown's OPA627' calls the sound refined and dynamic, and a Japanese Dr.DAC3 comparison (Shirokuma) reported less treble harshness than the OPA627. The ADA4637-1 is praised for DAC I/V stages. No independent distortion measurements (Groner, ASR) were found.
sonic_descriptors: less treble harshness than the OPA627 (Japanese blog)
typical_uses: OPA627 alternative in single-op-amp positions (needs an SOIC-to-DIP adapter)
DAC I/V conversion (ADA4637-1 only at a noise gain of 5 or greater)
op-amp rolling in DAC and headphone gear (e.g. Dr.DAC3)
low-bias-current transimpedance stages (e.g. open-hardware STM tunnelling amps using the ADA4637-1ARZ)
caveats: The ADA4637-1 is decompensated (stable only at a noise gain of 5 or greater). It is not a drop-in for unity-gain buffers or low-gain positions.
Single channel only; dual sockets need an adapter.
SOIC-8 and LFCSP-8 only, with no DIP. The LFCSP is impractical for hand-rolling.
The sonic claims are subjective forum and blog listening and were not re-verified in this pass.
The AN-1429 praise is vendor marketing.
No independent measurement data was found.

silicon_changes.when: PCN 14_0038 Rev. -, 13 Feb 2014 (date per search summary)
silicon_changes.identification: After the change, parts carry a laser-marked pin-1 indicator. Country of origin and date code would separate the assembly sites. Not verified for each part.
silicon_changes.summary: Amkor Philippines was qualified as the assembly site for 3x3 mm LFCSP products, with Amkor's standard bill of materials in a sawn-singulated leadframe and no BOM change. Pin 1 is laser marked. This is an assembly change, not a die change. Inclusion of the ADA4627-1/ADA4637-1 is not confirmed, and the change would apply only to the LFCSP, not to the SOIC ARZ/BRZ.
silicon_changes.audio_impact: None expected: same die, package assembly only.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low - assembly-only change, and only on the LFCSP, which is rarely used for rolling.
silicon_changes.verification: A search confirmed the PCN content (Amkor Philippines, 3x3 mm LFCSP, sawn, laser-marked pin 1, data-sheet function unaffected). The result did not confirm that ADA4627-1 or ADA4637-1 are on its parts list.

counterfeit_notes: No counterfeit reports were found; counterfeits were not searched this pass because of the search budget. The claim that the community prefers the part because, unlike the OPA627, it is not faked is low-confidence folklore. Buy from ADI or authorised distributors. Be wary of pre-mounted 'ADA4627 on DIP adapter' marketplace modules whose die provenance cannot be checked.

open_questions: Revision chain: Rev. F is current, and Rev. A exists as a copy. The letters and dates for Rev. 0 and B to E, the date printed on Rev. F, and the revision that merged the ADA4637-1 are unknown. Use Wayback on the legacy static ADA4627-1.pdf and the combined PDF.
Is the Octopart '36 V, 80 MHz' ADA4637 sheet a preliminary (Rev. PrA) or a released standalone datasheet?

36 V vs. 30 V: ADI's product page itself uses '36 V' (so it is not an Eagle transcription error), while the Rev. F title uses '30 V' and the operating range is ±5 V to ±15 V. Confirm that 36 V is the absolute-maximum rating.

Confirm the exact ADA4637-1 GBW (about 80 MHz from the title) and the ADA4627-1 slew rate (60 V/us per a search summary) against Table 1. Also check i_n, Iq, output current, THD+N, and Vos/Ib by A/B grade.

PCN applicability: PCN 14_0038 (3x3 mm LFCSP assembly move to Amkor Philippines) and PCN 17_0068 Rev. B (added ASE Korea assembly, later cancelled) surfaced in searches for these parts, but the affected-part lists were not seen. Newer PCNs 23_0149, 24_0009, 24_0206, 25_0091 and 26_0029 also surfaced, with unknown relevance. No die change or wafer-fab transfer is known.
Ordering codes ADA4627-1ARZ/BRZ/ACPZ and ADA4637-1ACPZ were not web-confirmed. The lifecycle status of all codes (active or NRND) is unconfirmed.
The LTspice ADA4637 macro-model fixes of 04/17/21 and 05/12/21 are simulation-model changes only, not silicon changes.
Forum and blog praise (diyAudio, head-fi, Shirokuma) was not re-verified this pass. No independent measurements (Groner, ASR) have been located.

revision_chain_notes:
Only one vendor document exists: the Analog Devices data sheet for ADA4627-1 / ADA4637-1, from a sole source with no second sources. Known chain, oldest to newest:
(1) Standalone ADA4627-1 sheet, 'ADA4627-1.pdf', titled '36 V, 19 MHz, Low Noise, Low Bias Current, JFET Op Amp'. It was published on or before 2009-12-22 and was probably Rev. 0 or preliminary; legacy URL http://www.analog.com/static/imported-files/data_sheets/ADA4627-1.pdf.
(2) Rev. A of the ADA4627-1 sheet, known only from the datasheetq copy slug; date unknown.
(3) Standalone ADA4637-1 sheet titled '36 V, 80 MHz ...' (Octopart copy), about 2010, possibly Rev. PrA.
(4) The merged ADA4627-1/ADA4637-1 sheet 'ADA4627-1_4637-1.pdf', later retitled '30 V, High Speed, Low Noise, Low Bias Current, JFET Operational Amplifier'. The current edition is Rev. F. Search summaries again gave '08/02/2010' for Rev. F, which is still doubtful for a sixth revision and probably a site metadata date.
This pass found no new revision letters or dates. A DigChip copy titled '36 V High Performance, JFET-...' may be an early or preliminary ADA4627-1 edition (inferred from the title; revision not shown).
Missing links: the printed date and D-code of every revision. Rev. 0 and Rev. A dates are unknown, and Revs. B, C, D and E are unknown, including which of them merged in the ADA4637-1 and changed 36 V to 30 V. The Rev. F date as printed and the page-2 revision-history table contents are also missing. The best way to fill these gaps is a Wayback lookup of the archive seed URLs: the legacy static/imported-files PDF and the old analog.com product-page paths.
